An ordinary conversational verb for objecting or raising an objection. The final ض is emphatic, and no MSA past-tense ending is pronounced.
The idiom describes someone tiresome, irritating, or unfunny. ق is glottalized, and دم has a doubled م.
Common in conversation for an agreement, especially a written agreement or treaty. The colloquial pronunciation glottalizes ق and ends in -iyye.
The usual word for a serving tray or oven pan. It has emphatic ص, long ii, and doubled ي.
A collective noun meaning clouds or cloud cover. The Palestinian vowel is long ee, not the MSA diphthong ay.
Commonly describes someone bold, daring, or brave. The long ii is followed by a final hamza.
The colloquial verb can have the i–i vocalization ghiDib. It is less frequent in everyday Ramallah speech than عصب or زعل.
The everyday word for a theater; it can also mean the stage. The final ح is pronounced 7.
Urban ق is glottalized. A short helping vowel is commonly heard before the final ر, though the final cluster can also remain unbroken.
Used conversationally for legendary or extraordinarily impressive. ط is emphatic, and the middle vowel is long uu.
A common loanword for a garage. Depending on context, it can also denote a vehicle workshop or parking facility.
An ordinary adjective for aggressive or hostile behavior. The unstressed initial vowel varies somewhat; i is a common colloquial realization.
Both ذ sounds are normally pronounced z in this word, hence the pronunciation respelling. It is used conversationally alongside زاكي for tasty or delicious.
The usual Palestinian word for a hammer. The vowels are aa and uu.
The b- marks the ordinary present tense, and the person prefix addresses a male. The verb retains doubled ت and has glottalized ق.
The masculine participle is the normal conversational way to ask whether someone is sure. Its internal hamza is pronounced, and ك is doubled.
The masculine active participle means coming or on the way. It ends in consonantal y after long aa.
After biddi, the first-person verb has no present-tense b- prefix. ق is glottalized in this conversational pronunciation.
This is the collective noun for dates. A short helping vowel is commonly pronounced between م and ر, although an unbroken final cluster is also possible.
A common blessing meaning may God make things easy. The optative verb has no b- prefix, and ه is doubled.
The first verb addresses a male and has glottalized ق. Doubled ل distinguishes teach from other readings of the unvowelled second verb.
The ordinary word for a butterfly. There is no doubled ر, and the feminine ending after ش is pronounced e.
